resources.string: Android must allow this app to install the small helper app that carries each package to the watch. Enable the permission, then come back and press the button again.

Apps this phone sent to the watch. "Send again" takes the package out of the helper app and sends it to the watch once more, e.g. after a failed delivery. Removing a helper app asks Galaxy Wearable to remove the app from the watch too, but it does not always do it. The app cannot check what is on the watch; the list in Galaxy Wearable is the reference.
Nothing sent yet. Helper apps made by older versions of this app are not shown; install the package again to see it here.
All sent apps are up to date.
Could not check %1$d apps: check the internet connection and try again.

Android will remove the helper app and Galaxy Wearable should remove the app from the watch. This does not always happen: afterwards check the app list in Galaxy Wearable and remove the app there if it is still on the watch.
Confirm the removal in the Android dialog…
Could not remove the helper app: %1$s
The helper app is removed. Galaxy Wearable should remove the app from the watch, but this does not always happen: check the app list in Galaxy Wearable.
Galaxy Wearable is not installed. It delivers packages to the watch and manages the watch.
Samsung\'s Gear Plugin is not installed. Galaxy Wearable adds it when you connect a Galaxy Watch or Gear watch: connect your watch there first.
Android must allow this app to install the small helper app that carries each package to the watch.
Tap to confirm the helper app that carries the package to the watch.
Waiting %1$d s so Galaxy Wearable can finish the previous package

Version %1$s, %2$s.\n\nThe package will be downloaded from the Tizen Archive catalog and sent to the watch through Galaxy Wearable. Android will ask you to confirm the installation of a small helper app.
Another installation is running. Wait for it to finish and open the link again.
The package was not found in the catalog.
Cannot reach the catalog. Check the internet connection and try again.
The catalog returned an unexpected answer.
The downloaded file does not match the catalog data and was discarded. Try again.
The package is too large for this app.
The file is not available for download.
The developer certificate is tied to specific watches.
The watch does not accept the signature of this package.
Compatibility with the watch is not confirmed.
Already sent on %1$s, skipped. Use “Send again” on the “On the watch” tab to send it anyway.
Confirm the installation on the phone
Installed on the phone; Galaxy Wearable sends it to the watch
A helper app for this package was installed with a different key. Uninstall it in Android settings first (this also removes the app from the watch), then try again.
Not signed by a distributor: the watch will most likely refuse this package.
The signature imitates a Samsung certificate authority but its certificate chain is not genuine: the watch will refuse the package.
Signed with a certificate that Tizen watches do not trust (Samsung VD or the Tizen SDK): the watch will refuse the package.
The developer certificate expired on %1$s: the watch will refuse the package.
Developer certificate for specific watches (%1$d listed), valid until %2$s: it installs only on those watches.
Developer certificate for specific watches, valid until %1$s: it installs only on those watches.
Removing a helper app from the phone may also remove the app from the watch, but Galaxy Wearable does not always do it. Check the app list in Galaxy Wearable.
Works without a computer or developer mode: Galaxy Wearable delivers each package over Bluetooth.

Faster and shows the real result, but needs developer mode on the watch: turn on Debugging (Settings → About watch → Software, tap the version 5 times; then Developer options → Debugging) and connect the watch to the same Wi-Fi network as the phone. The first time, the watch asks to allow this phone. No other sdb tool may be connected to the watch meanwhile.
On the watch: Settings → Connections → Wi-Fi → tap the network → scroll down to the IP address
Enter the IPv4 address of the watch in your home network, for example 192.168.0.20
The watch did not report a result
The phone is not connected to Wi-Fi
Cannot reach the watch. Check the address, that Wi-Fi and Debugging are on, wake the watch, and allow access to the local network for this app.
The watch closed the connection: another sdb tool (for example on a computer) is probably connected to it. Disconnect it and try again.
The watch did not confirm this phone in time. Tap Allow on the watch when it asks.
The watch did not accept this phone.
The watch stopped answering. Keep its screen on and try again.
The connection to the watch broke. Try again.
The watch answered in an unexpected way.
Looking for the watch in this Wi-Fi network…
Several devices answer; choose the watch:

No watch found. Wake the watch (keep its screen on), check that Wi-Fi and Debugging are on and that the phone and the watch use the same network, not a guest network, and turn off any VPN on the phone.
The phone is not connected to Wi-Fi.
This Wi-Fi network cannot be searched. Enter the address of the watch by hand.
Allow this app to use the local network (Android settings → Apps → this app → Permissions), otherwise the phone cannot see the watch.
Install again even if the watch already has the version
Already on the watch (v%1$s), skipped. Turn on “Install again even if the watch already has the version” to install it anyway.
System packages are listed too. Only packages installed by this app can be removed here; removing a package also deletes its data on the watch.
The app is removed from the watch together with its data. This cannot be undone.
The watch could not remove the app: %1$s
A queue is running: the way of sending cannot be changed now.
Enter the address of the watch
The address of the watch is not valid
Helper apps this phone sent through Galaxy Wearable
Packages the watch reports over Wi-Fi · %1$s
It will be installed over Wi-Fi on %1$s.
It will be installed through Galaxy Wearable.

While this is on, packages that Galaxy Wearable sends to the watch (installs from Galaxy Store, companion apps) are copied into the chosen folder, before the watch deletes them. Keep the watch screen on and install as usual. Only files are read on the watch; nothing is changed there.
The phone is not on Wi-Fi. Waiting for it…
Choose a folder on the Install tab first: packages are saved there.
Allow access to devices on the local network for this app.
The app may not write to the folder. Choose the folder again on the Install tab.
Saved as %1$s, but without the store signature: other watches will not accept it.
The watch was faster and deleted it before it was copied.
While saving is on, the list of packages on the watch is not available.
